$comment: Single source of truth for the gallery. Read by the skills, the installer, the test runner and the README. Adding a style means adding src/styles/<file>.ts, an entry here, and running `npm run build`.

categories.name: Git
categories.description: Branch, working tree state, worktrees and pull requests

categories.name: Usage
categories.description: Context window, tokens, session cost and rate limits

styles.name: Basic
styles.description: Model, directory, context usage and both rate-limit windows on one line.

styles.name: Compact
styles.description: Directory and context percentage only. No colors, no icons.

styles.name: Branch
styles.description: Directory and branch, with a single marker for uncommitted work.

styles.name: Full
styles.description: Branch, ahead/behind, conflict/staged/modified/untracked counts, worktree and open PR (clickable).

styles.name: Tokens
styles.description: Context bar plus token counts, aware of 200k vs 1M context windows.

styles.name: Cost tracker
styles.description: Session cost, duration, lines changed and rate limits with reset countdowns.

styles.name: Pace
styles.description: One line: directory, branch, context, and both rate-limit windows shown as where you are heading, not just where you are.

styles.name: Powerline
styles.description: Two rows of filled segments joined by powerline arrows: session and cost above, context and rate-limit gauges below. Requires a Nerd Font.

styles.name: Multiline
styles.description: Two lines: model, directory, git and PR above; context bar, cost and limits below.

styles.name: Dashboard
styles.description: Four lines. Context and both rate-limit windows as aligned bars on one scale, so you can see which runs out first, plus a projection of where each window is heading.
